See nitrogen research at Husker Harvest Days

Four demonstration plots will compare nitrogen management strategies to show farmers how digital tools can optimize fertilizer use and boost profitability.

Elizabeth Hodges,staff writer,Farm ProgressSeptember 10, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

With costly inputs being applied to fields, University of Nebraska-Lincoln researchers are looking into how to cut these costs. Dirk Charlson, Nebraska digital agriculture educator, is excited to showcase this nitrogen research along Flag Road. Kevin Schulz

Applying nitrogen too early, too late or in excessive amounts can harm not only yield and profitability, but also the surrounding environment.

With rising input costs, including fertilizer, University of Nebraska-Lincoln researchers are testing nitrogen scheduling tools in cornfields during Husker Harvest Days to determine which methods work best.

The demonstrations allow visitors to compare crop performance under each management approach and explore how data-driven nitrogen recommendations can optimize fertilizer use while maintaining crop productivity.

Determining the right timing and application rates doesn’t have to be guesswork. Dirk Charlson, Nebraska digital agriculture educator, hopes this demonstration will show how digital tools can help farmers make better management decisions.

“We’ll use those tools to help us figure out how much nitrogen to apply and then when to apply the nitrogen when the plants need it,” Charlson said.

Related:Experience corn harvest equipment up close at Husker Harvest Days

UNL’s Dirk Charlson and his team will demonstrate nitrogen research as well as how drones can be used for agronomic practices such as making stand counts. Pictured is an aerial view of the research field at HHD. (Dirk Charlson)

Answering real-world questions

Attendees at this year’s HHD can explore four nitrogen management demonstration plots located along Flag Road. The plots highlight decision-support tools designed to improve nitrogen management, including the UNL nitrogen calculator and nitrogen scheduling recommendations from Sentinel Fertigation.

A reference plot received the nitrogen rate recommended by the UNL nitrogen calculator and is being compared with plots receiving an additional 50 and 100 pounds of nitrogen per acre, as well as a plot managed using Sentinel Fertigation’s nitrogen scheduling recommendations.

No producer wants to waste costly inputs through runoff or leaching. With environmental and economic concerns in mind, farmers can achieve a win-win through accurate nitrogen application. Charlson said most farmers probably apply more nitrogen than plants need, raising concerns about groundwater.

Economics also plays a major role in on-farm decisions. “It’s very clear, the two biggest expenses are seed and nitrogen. So, anything that we can do to help farmers figure out how to reduce costs associated with those can have significant impact,” Charlson said.

In addition to the plots, several innovative programs will be highlighted, such as ScoutNebraska and On-Farm Research Network. Nebraska Extension educators and specialists will be available to answer questions in the field or at the Big Red Building at Lot 827.

At the research site, Charlson will also demonstrate his recent work using drones for stand counts. This technology helps producers make more informed decisions by providing visual data.

Related:HHD food drive has impact on local communities

“We will have a demonstration of how we can use a drone to look at plants, and that’s, of course, the first step toward doing things like stand counts,” Charlson said. “That’ll be one of the demonstrations and potentially will let producers try flying the drone.”

By addressing real farmers’ questions through field testing, Nebraska Extension educators bring practical information to Husker Harvest Days to boost profitability. Stop by the Flag Road research plots for more insights.

About the Author

Elizabeth Hodges

staff writer, Farm Progress

Growing up on a third-generation purebred Berkshire hog operation, Elizabeth Hodges of Julian, Neb., credits her farm background for showing her what it takes to be involved in the ag industry. She began her journalism career in high school, reporting on producer progress for the Midwest Messenger newspaper.

While a student at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, she became a Husker Harvest Days intern at Nebraska Farmer in 2022. The next year, she was hired full-time as a staff writer for Farm Progress. Elizabeth graduated from UNL in 2024 with a double major in Agriculture and Environmental Sciences Communication and Animal Science.Hodges’ father, Michael, raises purebred Berkshire hogs, and her mother, Christy, is an ag education teacher and FFA advisor at Johnson County Central. Hodges is the oldest sibling of four.

translationZh:
随着农田投入品成本不断攀升，内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的研究人员正在探索如何削减这些成本。内布拉斯加数字农业教育工作者Dirk Charlson对在Flag Road沿线展示这项氮肥研究感到兴奋。

过早、过晚或过量施用氮肥不仅会损害产量和盈利能力，还会对周边环境造成危害。

随着包括化肥在内的投入成本不断上涨，内布拉斯加大学林肯分校的研究人员正在Husker Harvest Days期间在玉米田测试氮肥调度工具，以确定哪种方法效果最佳。

这些示范活动让参观者能够比较每种管理方式下的作物表现，并探索数据驱动的氮肥推荐方案如何在保持作物生产力的同时优化肥料使用。

确定正确的施用时机和用量不必靠猜测。内布拉斯加数字农业教育工作者Dirk Charlson希望这次示范能展示数字工具如何帮助农民做出更好的管理决策。

"我们将利用这些工具来帮助我们确定该施多少氮肥，以及什么时候在植物需要的时候施用氮肥，"Charlson说。

**回答现实世界的问题**

今年HHD的参观者可以探索位于Flag Road沿线的四个氮肥管理示范田。这些示范田展示了旨在改善氮肥管理的决策支持工具，包括UNL氮肥计算器和Sentinel Fertigation的氮肥调度建议。

一个参照田块施用了UNL氮肥计算器推荐的氮肥用量，并与额外增施50磅和100磅氮肥/英亩的田块，以及采用Sentinel Fertigation氮肥调度建议管理的田块进行对比。

没有生产者愿意让昂贵的投入品通过径流或淋溶白白浪费。考虑到环境和经济方面的担忧，农民可以通过精准施氮实现双赢。Charlson表示，大多数农民可能施用的氮肥超过了植物所需，这引发了对地下水的担忧。

经济因素在农场决策中也起着重要作用。"很明显，最大的两项支出是种子和氮肥。所以，我们能为农民做的任何帮助他们降低这些成本的事情，都能产生显著影响，"Charlson说。

除了这些示范田，还将重点介绍几个创新项目，如ScoutNebraska和On-Farm Research Network。内布拉斯加推广部门的教育工作者和专家将在田间或827号展位的大红楼（Big Red Building）回答问题。

在研究现场，Charlson还将展示他最近使用无人机进行株数统计的工作。这项技术通过提供可视化数据，帮助生产者做出更明智的决策。

"我们将演示如何使用无人机观察植物，这当然是进行株数统计等工作的第一步，"Charlson说。"这将是其中一项演示，可能会让生产者尝试操作无人机。"

通过田间测试回答农民的实际问题，内布拉斯加推广部门的教育工作者将实用信息带到Husker Harvest Days，以提升盈利能力。欢迎前往Flag Road研究示范田了解更多见解。
